main_text.l: הִתְפָּרְקוּ Abruperunt sibi, sive, Detraxerunt inaures aureas, Exod.32.24.
פֶּרֶק m. Diruptio, Dilaceratio, Laceratum, Nah.3.1. At Obad.14. ab Hebraeis exponitur Compitum, quasi via Disruptio. Rabbini Caput libri sic vocant.
פָּרָק m. Frustum: Constr. וּפֶרֶק פִּגּוּלִים[?] Et fragmen sive Frustum carnium abominandarum, Esa.65.4. pro quo legendum juxta Masorethas, ומרק. Vide מָרַק.
מִפְרַקְתָּא f. Cervix, Corpages vertebrarum cervicis, à nodis & Interruptionibus sic dicta: Aff. אֶת־מִפְרַקְתּוֹ Cervicem suam, 1.Sam.4.18.
פָּרוּר m. Cacabus, Num.11.8. בְּפָרוּר In cacabo, Jud.6.19. Cum epenthesi, פָּאֲרוּר[?] Nigror olivaris[?], Pallor livens; juxta R.Salomonem, Joel.2.6. at juxta R.Aben Esram est à פאר. Vide istic.

פֵּרַשׁ Expositum fuit. Exposuit, Explanavit, Declaravit, Explicuit: Infinit. לְפָרֵשׁ לָהֶם Ad exponendum eis, Lev.24.12. Niph. נִפְרַשׁ Separari, Dispergi, Dissipari. Particip. צֹאנוֹ נִפְרָשׁוֹת Ovium suarum dispersarum, Ezech.34.12. Pyh. Praeteritum, פֹּרַשׁ Expositum fuit, Num.15.34. Particip. מְפֹרָשׁ Explanatum, loco adverbii, Explanate, Nehem.8.8. Chald. מְפָרַשׁ Explicate, Esr.4.18. Hiph. ex alia significatione, Futurum, יְפָרֵשׁ Pungeet, Prov.23.32.

פָּרָשׁ masc. Eques, quòd equum calcaribus (quæ & hinc פָּרוּשִׁים Rabbinis dicuntur) pungat, Nah.3.2[?]. Ab. Esra scribit Prov.23.32: פָּרָשׁ dicitur בְּעֲבוּר הַפָּרָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלָיו à calcaribus quæ sunt in pedibus ejus. Et in Pathach, פָּרַשׁ Equitum, Ezech.26.10. ex forma dagessata, שַׁדִּי פַּנּ. Plural. פָּרָשִׁים Equites, Gen.50.9. Aff. וּפָרָשָׁיו Et equitibus suis, Jesa.28.28. Kimchi, Cuspidibus sive Dentibus illius, scil. הַחָרוּץ Tribula, quæ sunt acuta & pungentes.
